extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners evaluating U.S. patent eligibility
extracted.subtask_description: Applying the Alice/Mayo two-step patent-eligibility framework (MPEP 2106) to determine whether claims are directed to judicial exceptions and, if so, whether they recite an inventive concept (significantly more). The sheet lists MPEP citations and illustrative case decisions holding claims eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim is not directed to an abstract idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims eligible in Step 2A: Claim is not directed to an abstract idea. See MPEP 2106.04(a), 2106.04(a)(1) and 2106.06(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative decisions holding claims not directed to an abstract idea include: Core Wireless (GUI for mobile devices that displays commonly accessed data on main menu) — see April 2, 2018 Memo; DDR Holdings (matching website 'look and feel') — see Example 2; Enfish (self-referential data table); Finjan v. Blue Coat Sys. (virus scan that generates a security profile identifying both hostile and potentially hostile operations) — see April 2, 2018 Memo; McRO (rules for lip sync and facial expression animation); Thales Visionix (using sensors to more efficiently track an object on a moving platform); Trading Tech. v. CQG (GUI that prevents order entry at a changed price); Visual Memory (enhanced computer memory system). These examples illustrate factual situations where courts found claims were not 'directed to' the abstract-idea exception under Step 2A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim is not directed to a product of nature (markedly different characteristics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims eligible in Step 2A when the claimed nature-based product has markedly different characteristics from the naturally occurring counterpart. See MPEP 2106.04(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative decisions: Chakrabarty (genetically modified bacterium) — see Example 13 (NBP-5); Myriad (cDNA with modified nucleotide sequence) — see Example 15 (NBP-7). The key evaluative point is whether the claimed product exhibits 'markedly different characteristics' relative to the natural product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim is not directed to a law of nature or natural phenomenon
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims eligible in Step 2A where the claim is not directed to a law of nature or natural phenomenon. See MPEP 2106.04(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative decisions and examples include: Eibel Process (gravity-fed paper machine) — see Example 32; Rapid Litigation Management v. CellzDirect (cryopreserving liver cells); Tilghman (method of hydrolyzing fat) — see Example 33; Vanda Pharm. (identifying patients who metabolize a drug poorly, and administering an adjusted dose of the drug to such patients) — see June 7, 2018 Memo; screening method using transformed cells. These examples demonstrate situations where courts found claims not to be directed to a law of nature or natural phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim as a whole amounts to significantly more than the recited judicial exception (inventive concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims eligible in Step 2B when the claim, taken as a whole, amounts to significantly more than the recited judicial exception — i.e., the claim recites an inventive concept. See MPEP 2106.05 and 2106.05(a) through (h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative decisions holding claims eligible under Step 2B include: Abele (tomographic scanning); Amdocs (field enhancement in distributed network); BASCOM (filtering Internet content) — see Example 34; Classen; Myriad CAFC (processing data about vaccination schedules & then vaccinating); Diehr; RCT (rubber manufacturing) — see Example 25; Exergen v. Kaz (measuring core body temperature); Mackay Radio (antenna); SiRF Tech (GPS system) (digital image processing) — see Example 3 and Example 4. Note: '†' indicates a non-precedential decision issued with a written opinion. These cases illustrate how courts have found that particular additional claim elements or combination of elements provide 'significantly more' than the judicial exception.
